prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, from heterobifunctional PROTACs that recruit ubiquitin ligases to the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type glue degraders

statement.case_for: I have moved from nanopores to targeted protein degradation. The principle can be said in one sentence: a small molecule that holds a chosen protein next to a ubiquitin ligase converts a cellular process into a chemical reaction under design control. It is also a case where the physical mechanism has been measured and not inferred, through ternary-complex co-crystal structures and cooperativity data, and the generative potential is real, since it reaches targets that inhibitors cannot. The three names map onto separable steps that can be defended to a broad audience: Crews and Deshaies for the heterobifunctional concept and its first demonstration in cells, and Handa for identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explained a drug action that was a mystery for decades. It is the only shortlisted candidate that all eight members ranked, and four members now propose the identical trio.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved, so the heterobifunctional branch is clinically unproven, and the approved imid drugs were found empirically; the prize would reward a concept and a mechanism more than a finished modality. Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex design) and Sakamoto (first PROTAC paper) have serious claims, and I cannot rule out that the trio is contested. The citation must hold two lines, PROTACs and cereblon, under one idea, induced proximity, and I accept that this is a judgement and not an obvious fit. Finally, a fair reader can call it pharmacology and chemical biology more than chemistry.

responses.point: B056 is the clearest game-changer on the list, and breadth of ranking is a reason to defend it publicly, but the record of the 2001 PROTAC paper and the cereblon work must be checked.
responses.response: Johan, your argument that mechanism, design principle and clinical entry hold together moved me, and your remark that Handa was named third in six of eight openings is the strongest answer to Ciulli. I still want the priority record on the 2001 paper checked before the vote, since that decides whether Sakamoto's role makes the trio vulnerable. I also keep your B058 as my second alternative. Its attribution is the cleanest on the list, but I judge that a computational methods prize is harder to explain beyond the field than a new modality, so I do not place it first.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B056 first but says the cereblon and glue side is better established than the PROTAC side and wants the citation to rest on mechanism and structure.
responses.response: Andrei, I agree and have written my citation so that it rests on induced proximity as the shared mechanism, with cereblon named explicitly because that is where the structural and clinical evidence is firmest. My answer to your two-lines worry is that the citation does not claim one discovery; it credits a concept and a target identification that together established the modality. If you would rather narrow the PROTAC claim to demonstrated degradation in cells and ternary-complex structures, I would accept that wording. On your question of what would move me to B019, a convincing account that the lipidoid screening line, and not the Vancouver chemistry, was decisive, together with a clean three-name set.

responses.point: Zou moved to B056, stresses ternary-complex crystal structures as the best evidence, and is uneasy that Ciulli is left out.
responses.response: Xiaodong, the structural evidence is what changes my view, because it supplies the physical, atomic-level mechanism that I look for and that I could not find in the nanopore case. I share your unease about Ciulli, but his work is the VHL ligand and ternary-complex design line, and the committee cannot add a fourth name. The test I would apply is who established the concept and who identified the target, and on that test Crews, Deshaies and Handa stand. If the expert reports show Ciulli's contribution to be the decisive step in making degraders rational, I would revisit the trio.

responses.point: Aili and Sparr prefer B019 and ask whether the decisive step was Vancouver encapsulation chemistry or lipid screening, and whether the 2023 Medicine prize makes the area feel honoured.
responses.response: Daniel, I take the impact point seriously, and B019 stays outside my preferred configuration for attribution, not for science: the trios proposed in the committee differ (Anderson versus Hope) and neither of us has verified patent priority. I do not read the 2023 Medicine prize as a bar. I would be glad to see the committee answer the decisive-step question, because if it resolves clearly in one direction, B019 becomes a serious competitor, but with a three-name limit I cannot yet defend a cut that leaves out Hope or Anderson.

responses.point: Sparr frames B019 as phase behaviour and self-assembly and concedes that she may overweight that explanation.
responses.response: Emma, I appreciate the physical-chemistry framing, and your candid statement that your name choice would shift to Anderson if the decisive step were library design shows exactly why the trio is not settled. That uncertainty is my reason for not moving to B019. I do not regard B056 as the lesser physical-chemistry case, since cooperativity in ternary complexes is the same sort of quantitative thermodynamic argument.

responses.point: Somfai holds B016 as mature, cleanly attributed and arguably overdue, and asks what was chemically new in degradation.
responses.response: Peter, I agree B016 is mature and well attributed, and the 2010 prize question is real. What I find decisive is that induced proximity is a new capability, small-molecule control of protein lifetime, while C-N coupling extends a known logic to a new nucleophile. Your question of what is chemically new is answered by heterobifunctional design and the discovery of ligands for E3 ligases, which is molecular design and not only biology. I would keep B016 as a candidate for a later year, and I do not list it among my alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts PROTACs and molecular glues as one achievement under induced proximity, and whether the absence of an approved PROTAC makes the prize premature.
Whether the priority record on the first PROTAC paper makes the trio without Sakamoto or Ciulli defensible.
Whether the committee will resolve the decisive-step question for B019 clearly enough that it becomes a better-attributed competitor.

Whether nanopore sensing (B017) belongs to chemistry, and whether the omission of Branton and Kasianowicz can be justified; this remains my reason for placing it as an alternative and not a first choice.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited name; I am a nanophysicist at Lund University, and my work on molecular motors and nanowire devices has no stated connection to the degrader, nanopore, lipid nanoparticle or other investigators. Somfai and Sparr are also at Lund, which is not a conflict for any candidate. As chair I have moved my preference away from the nanopore candidate on the merits, and I do not treat support counts as a substitute for that judgement.
